$comment: Suggestion Review Board. Nothing here is a plan until a row is ticked. Status meanings: shipped = built in this branch; in progress = being built now; awaiting decision = a human must choose; proposed = not started; needs review = shipped but carrying an open flag.
how_to_read: Each row states the problem it solves, the change, why it is worth doing now, what it costs, what could go wrong, and which decision it unblocks. Effort is one dev-day unit: S ≈ under an hour, M ≈ half a day, L ≈ a day or more.

paths.name: Look like a shop this week
paths.for_whom: You want the URL to be shareable before it earns anything.
paths.exit_criteria: A reader who has never seen the repo can name the section they are in, find a guide in two clicks, and never reads a row of internal vocabulary. Zero broken links, disclosure present on 100% of pages.
paths.what_you_get_measured: Organic entrance pages and scroll depth only — no revenue signal is available before PATH-B.
paths.risk: Polish without listings can look like an empty shop; mitigate by keeping the locked shelf visible and honest about why.

paths.name: Unlock the money path first
paths.for_whom: You have a live Associates account and the 180-day clock is running.
paths.exit_criteria: Five verified /dp/ listings in the register, one tagged link per product tested end to end (destination + click counted in Associates reporting), gate green, links live.
paths.what_you_get_measured: Clicks and orders from Associates Central — the only authorized source of truth for money.
paths.risk: Publishing links before the account is accepted wastes nothing but also earns nothing; check account state first (Q-03).

paths.name: Compound the traffic
paths.for_whom: The site is live and you can commit real hours weekly to editorial.
paths.exit_criteria: Two guides per week for six weeks, every guide in the sitemap and feed within an hour of publish, Search Console verified with a query export feeding the next topic choice.
paths.what_you_get_measured: Impressions and queries by page, outbound CTR by slot, signup rate on the capture block.
paths.risk: Cadence is the whole bet; a missed fortnight turns this back into PATH-A.

suggestions.title: Rebuild the landing page as a publication front page
suggestions.problem: A first-time visitor landed on registers, status vocabulary and verification scaffolding — an audit, not a shop.
suggestions.change: Masthead, lead story, section rail, product shelf, question-shaped guide cards, small transparency strip. Dashboards move to one nav group and the footer.
suggestions.why_now: Every share, every first organic visit and every judge of the application sees this page first.
suggestions.risk: Reader pages must still carry the disclosure; the gate checks order, not just presence.
suggestions.unlocks: Anyone can link to the homepage without an explanation attached.

suggestions.title: Disclosure strip under the masthead on every page, repeated in the footer
suggestions.problem: Commission disclosure that lives only on a policy page fails the conspicuousness test people actually apply.
suggestions.change: A persistent strip carrying the exact Operating Agreement sentence plus a plain-language line, adjacent to the first product link on article pages, with a link to /disclosure/.
suggestions.why_now: It is a contractual obligation, not a style choice, and it costs nothing to do properly the first time.
suggestions.risk: Over-styling it (tiny contrast, hairline text) defeats the purpose; the gate asserts a minimum size and contrast.
suggestions.unlocks: Compliance question closed for every page including new ones.

suggestions.title: Product cards that show the register, not a fake buy button
suggestions.problem: There is no verified listing to send a reader to; a button that 404s burns the only asset a small site has.
suggestions.change: Cards render title/price/rating as an explicit em-dash with “not verified”, plus the reason and the fix, in a locked state.
suggestions.why_now: It is the only presentation that is both honest and still useful to the reader.
suggestions.risk: Looks unfinished — which it is; the copy says so once and moves on.
suggestions.unlocks: Nothing to retract when listings arrive; the card just fills in.

suggestions.title: Ban audit vocabulary from reader pages
suggestions.problem: Words like ASIN, register, provenance and flag IDs in buyer copy read as machine output.
suggestions.change: Reader-facing templates never print internal IDs; the same facts sit in /verify/ and /dashboard/ tables. A banned-word list is enforced by the gate.
suggestions.why_now: Cheapest trust win available; zero editorial cost.
suggestions.risk: Over-sanitising hides the honest limits — so each article still ends with “What we did not check”.
suggestions.unlocks: Pages read like a magazine.

suggestions.title: Section pages open on the buyer's question
suggestions.problem: Category descriptions are a directory convention; nobody browses a category page for its own sake.
suggestions.change: Each section leads with the question it answers and the comparison list, then the shelf.
suggestions.why_now: It doubles as the answer box search engines like.
suggestions.risk: Low.
suggestions.unlocks: Long-tail queries phrased as questions get a page that matches them.

suggestions.title: Two calculators the reader controls
suggestions.problem: Buyers cannot judge running cost or counter fit from a spec table alone.
suggestions.change: Cost-to-run and counter-footprint tools that compute only from the reader's own inputs, showing the arithmetic, with no appliance figures invented.
suggestions.why_now: Interactive tools earn links and repeat visits without needing product data we do not have.
suggestions.risk: Any default must be labelled as an example, never as a product spec.
suggestions.unlocks: Time-on-page and a defensible reason to be bookmarked.

suggestions.title: Typography, measure, dark mode, print sheet
suggestions.problem: Wall-of-text rendering is the visual signature of generated content.
suggestions.change: Serif display + humanist body, 68ch measure, real spacing scale, prefers-color-scheme support, and a print stylesheet so a checklist can go to the shop.
suggestions.why_now: Print-friendly checklists are how a buying guide gets carried, which is how it gets remembered.
suggestions.risk: Low.
suggestions.unlocks: Reader comfort + the comparison sheet.

suggestions.title: Comparison sheet the reader fills in
suggestions.problem: The decision happens in a shop aisle or a group chat, not on a page.
suggestions.change: A printable comparison sheet generated from each section's compare-on list, with blank columns for the models actually under consideration.
suggestions.why_now: It converts reading into a decision, which is what a shop exists for.
suggestions.risk: It must not pre-fill competitor claims we cannot source.
suggestions.unlocks: Genuine utility; the kind of page people send to each other.

suggestions.title: One site to index: canonical URLs, no parameter sprawl
suggestions.problem: Two URLs per page (index.html and directory path) splits credit and looks like duplication.
suggestions.change: Every page gets one canonical, trailing-slash directory URLs, relative asset paths so the same build works on any host, robots.txt pointing at the sitemap.
suggestions.why_now: Before a crawler arrives is the only cheap time to set this.
suggestions.risk: Custom domain later changes only config.baseUrl.
suggestions.unlocks: Clean index state.

suggestions.title: Question-shaped titles matched to question-shaped answers
suggestions.problem: Broad head terms are unwinnable for a new site with no links.
suggestions.change: Publish against specific phrasings (“what should you compare”, “how to assess cleanup”) and answer the question inside the first screenful.
suggestions.why_now: A new domain wins on specificity or not at all.
suggestions.risk: Titles are hypotheses until measured — see FLG-005; do not describe them as popular.
suggestions.unlocks: The first real query data.

suggestions.title: Structured data that only describes what we can show
suggestions.problem: Review and Product markup with invented ratingValue is a manual-action magnet and a lie.
suggestions.change: Emit Article, BreadcrumbList, and FAQPage; no aggregateRating, no Offer, no price, until a listing is verified.
suggestions.why_now: Markup is easy to add and dangerous to backfill.
suggestions.risk: Under-claiming, which is the safe direction.
suggestions.unlocks: Rich-result eligibility without fake stars.

suggestions.title: Sitemap + RSS that the build regenerates
suggestions.problem: Hand-maintained feeds drift the moment anyone publishes.
suggestions.change: sitemap.xml and feed.xml generated from the guide index on every build, with lastmod from the review date; the gate fails on drift.
suggestions.why_now: It is the plumbing that makes a publishing cadence possible.
suggestions.risk: Low.
suggestions.unlocks: New guides go out to subscribers and crawlers without a second task.

suggestions.title: Client-side site search over a static index
suggestions.problem: A publication with six guides already needs search, and Pages has no server to query.
suggestions.change: search.json built at generate time + a small filter UI; no third-party search widget.
suggestions.why_now: Keeps the search box honest and dependency-free.
suggestions.risk: Not fuzzy; acceptable at this size.
suggestions.unlocks: Lower bounce on section pages.

suggestions.title: Set the cadence before the tooling needs it
suggestions.problem: Unstated cadence means no one can tell whether the site is alive or abandoned.
suggestions.change: Two guides a week, Fridays, with a written queue of twelve titles and a review date on each published piece.
suggestions.why_now: The 180-day review window makes recency structural, not cosmetic: Amazon's own criteria ask for content within roughly 60 days.
suggestions.risk: Cadence is a promise to the reader and to whoever maintains this; propose it, then only ship what you will sustain.
suggestions.unlocks: SG-15..SG-20 automation only pays off against a repeatable rhythm.

suggestions.title: Collector that refuses to invent
suggestions.problem: Automated product research fails at the step where a missing field gets guessed.
suggestions.change: tools/collect.mjs reads PA-API or hand-pasted listing JSON from data/inbox/, writes only fields present in the source, stamps each field with its origin, and records a diff instead of overwriting silently.
suggestions.why_now: It is the only automation that touches money, so build it before the volume exists.
suggestions.risk: Garbage in stays garbage; the collector validates format and nothing more.
suggestions.unlocks: Adding a tenth product costs a paste, not a rewrite.

suggestions.title: Link validator as a build step, not a habit
suggestions.problem: One mistagged link on one page is enough to lose attribution or breach policy.
suggestions.change: tools/validate-links.mjs checks ASIN shape, /dp/ structure, tag presence and placement, rel qualification, host allow-list, and every internal href against the built tree.
suggestions.why_now: Zero live links today makes this free to enforce forever.
suggestions.risk: False confidence on host allow-list — Amazon adds hosts; keep the list in config.
suggestions.unlocks: Scaling links becomes a merge, not an audit.

suggestions.title: Compliance gate that can fail the publish
suggestions.problem: Policies that live in a document get forgotten; policies that fail a build do not.
suggestions.change: tools/compliance-gate.mjs asserts disclosure presence, order before first product link, exact statement wording, no invented product claims, no banned superlatives, no untagged Amazon link, no link.amazon anywhere, alt text, canonical/OG parity, feed and sitemap freshness.
suggestions.why_now: The site's own claims about being careful become checkable.
suggestions.risk: Gate fatigue — keep every check able to produce a fix line, not a mystery.
suggestions.unlocks: Anyone can publish without memorising the agreement.

suggestions.title: Drift watch on the source register
suggestions.problem: Cited policy pages get revised; quotes go stale silently.
suggestions.change: npm run check:data compares each row in data/sources.json with its retrieval date and flags anything older than 90 days; --refresh-sources re-fetches and diffs.
suggestions.why_now: The register is the site's load-bearing claim; staleness turns it into a liability.
suggestions.risk: Network-dependent re-checks must degrade to a warning, not a hard fail.
suggestions.unlocks: Compliance review becomes a five-minute monthly task.

suggestions.title: Publish pipeline with a human checkpoint
suggestions.problem: “Fully automated publishing” on affiliate content means automated claims, which is exactly the failure mode this site is built to avoid.
suggestions.change: Documented pipeline: research → verify → draft → gate → publish → measure, with two human checkpoints (listing confirmation, claim approval) that cannot be skipped by configuration.
suggestions.why_now: Writing the boundary down now stops a future session automating the wrong part.
suggestions.risk: Two checkpoints slow output on purpose.
suggestions.unlocks: Automation where it is safe, judgment where it is not.

suggestions.title: CI on every push, Pages deploy on merge only
suggestions.problem: A broken main branch is the one state a reader can actually see.
suggestions.change: GitHub Actions runs check:data, build, validate-links, compliance-gate on PRs; publishing stays branch-and-folder so a failed check cannot ship.
suggestions.why_now: Free to set up while the repo is small.
suggestions.risk: Actions minutes are trivial at this size.
suggestions.unlocks: Merging without fear.

suggestions.title: Outbound-click counting without a person behind it
suggestions.problem: Per-user tagging of Associates links is prohibited, and a small site has no business building profiles.
suggestions.change: Aggregate-by-day counters keyed by page + product + slot; no cookie, no IP retained, no join possible.
suggestions.why_now: Designing the metric privacy-first is cheaper than retrofitting it.
suggestions.risk: Undercounting versus JS-blocked visitors — accept and state it.
suggestions.unlocks: CTR per slot without a compliance problem.

suggestions.title: Self-hosted endpoint reference implementation
suggestions.problem: The measurement plan needs a runtime GitHub Pages does not have.
suggestions.change: tools/analytics-server.mjs: /c/:id redirect, /e event sink, /summary JSON, day-bucketed files, rate limit, HMAC-signed link ids; runnable locally with no dependencies.
suggestions.why_now: Proves the design works before choosing a host.
suggestions.risk: Do not paste Associates secrets into it.
suggestions.unlocks: Q-09 becomes a hosting choice, not a research task.

suggestions.title: Campaign ledger with provenance or nothing
suggestions.problem: Affiliate dashboards fill up with modelled numbers that later get quoted as measured ones.
suggestions.change: data/campaign-ledger.json with fixed columns, allowed-source list, null≠0 semantics, and a provenance field per row; render-time derived metrics print a dash unless every input is real.
suggestions.why_now: An empty, well-defined ledger is the honest starting state.
suggestions.risk: Tempting to backfill — the validator blocks a row without a source.
suggestions.unlocks: Every future optimization decision has a dateable input.

suggestions.title: Join Search Console to the ledger for topic choice
suggestions.problem: Picking the next guide by instinct is how a niche site produces 40 unread posts.
suggestions.change: tools/next-topics.mjs reads a Performance export from data/exports/ and ranks candidate titles by impressions on queries we already appear for but do not answer; empty export ⇒ prints the manual method and refuses to guess.
suggestions.why_now: It needs to exist before the first export arrives.
suggestions.risk: Position data at 100 rows is noisy; require a minimum threshold before acting.
suggestions.unlocks: Measured queries pick the next topic.

suggestions.title: Fix the five identifiers, then test one link per product
suggestions.problem: Nothing monetizable exists: all five submitted identifiers are 9 characters and no listing is resolved.
suggestions.change: Replace with real 10-character ASINs, build exactly one tagged link per product in Associates Central, click it logged out, confirm destination and that the click shows in reporting, then scale to the rest.
suggestions.why_now: This single step is the difference between a mock-up and a business; it is also the only task that cannot be automated from here.
suggestions.risk: Scaling before the test risks five wrong links instead of one.
suggestions.unlocks: Everything money-related.

suggestions.title: Move off a github.io sub-path before submitting the site
suggestions.problem: Amazon's published review criteria include “You must own your website”, and a rejected application is not re-assessed.
suggestions.change: Buy the domain, point Pages at it, rebuild with config.baseUrl set, submit the property, keep the Pages URL as staging.
suggestions.why_now: Cheaper than losing the account cycle.
suggestions.risk: DNS and HTTPS propagation; do it once, verify once.
suggestions.unlocks: A defensible application and a brandable URL.

suggestions.title: Navigation labels a reader would use
suggestions.problem: Section and nav labels read like internal taxonomy (“Dashboard”, “Registers”).
suggestions.change: Reader vocabulary: Guides, Air Fryers, Multi-Cookers, Cleanup & Counter, Kitchen Basics, plus one “Inside the numbers” group for the operations surfaces; aria-current on the active item.
suggestions.why_now: It is the difference between a publication and an admin tool, and it is a label change.
suggestions.risk: Do not hide the dashboards — keep them one click away for the owner.
suggestions.unlocks: Orientation on first paint.

suggestions.title: RSS feed shipped, not promised
suggestions.problem: A feed link that 404s is worse than no feed.
suggestions.change: feed.xml generated with the guide index, correct pubDate/lastBuildDate, absolute links, and a link in the head and footer.
suggestions.why_now: It also gives a second discovery path besides search.
suggestions.risk: Feed must never list a draft; the generator only walks published guides.
suggestions.unlocks: Subscribers and a sanity check on publishing.

suggestions.title: Search Console verification and sitemap submission
suggestions.problem: Without it, there is no query data and no index visibility; every topic decision stays a guess.
suggestions.change: Verify the property (DNS or file upload), submit sitemap.xml, watch coverage, then export queries into data/exports/.
suggestions.why_now: Verification takes minutes and the data only starts accruing afterwards.
suggestions.risk: Cannot be done from this sandbox — it requires the owner's account (T-18).
suggestions.unlocks: PATH-C entirely.

suggestions.title: Reader capture with nowhere illegal to send it
suggestions.problem: An email form without a stated processor and policy is a compliance hole, not a growth feature.
suggestions.change: Capture block designed and disabled, with the “not wired” state visible; enabling it requires config + a privacy page naming the processor + double opt-in.
suggestions.why_now: Building it disabled costs nothing and prevents a future rushed yes.
suggestions.risk: Never store addresses in the repo — that is public.
suggestions.unlocks: Repeat audience independent of Google.

suggestions.title: Authorship that is true
suggestions.problem: A fake expert byline is the classic affiliate-site tell, and a fabricated endorsement.
suggestions.change: Desk byline, an explicit “AI-drafted, human-edited, nothing tested” note on each guide, and a /editorial-standards/ page stating what we do and do not do; upgrade to a named editor when a real person accepts (FLG-010).
suggestions.why_now: Honest authorship beats fake authority on trust and on policy.
suggestions.risk: Less persuasive than a fake PhD — on purpose.
suggestions.unlocks: Defensibility.

suggestions.title: Seasonal clusters that are dated, not seasonal-deal-shaped
suggestions.problem: A new site with no inventory has no business promising deal roundups.
suggestions.change: Season pages assemble existing guides by when the question gets asked (holiday cooking, summer grilling, back-to-dorm), with a review date on each and no price or availability claim.
suggestions.why_now: Clusters are how a small site gets topical depth in the eyes of a crawler.
suggestions.risk: Seasonal pages go stale loudly; every one carries a last-reviewed line.
suggestions.unlocks: Internal linking and topical coherence.

suggestions.title: Imagery labelled as what it is
suggestions.problem: Stock-looking or product-lookalike images imply experience we do not have.
suggestions.change: Generated editorial illustrations with captions that say illustration, no product depictions, no test-kitchen staging.
suggestions.why_now: Prevents a trust problem that would otherwise be baked into the template.
suggestions.risk: Illustrations must not resemble a specific brand's product.
suggestions.unlocks: Visual identity without deception.

suggestions.title: Brand system in one file
suggestions.problem: Name, tone and palette spread through templates cannot be swapped when FLG-009 resolves.
suggestions.change: Everything brand-related lives in config/site.config.json and one CSS custom-property block.
suggestions.why_now: The name is not cleared yet; make it one-line changeable.
suggestions.risk: None.
suggestions.unlocks: Rebrand in an afternoon.

suggestions.title: Ask the eight questions that gate every decision
suggestions.problem: Decisions are being made against information the owner has and the builder does not.
suggestions.change: /decision-brief/ with Q-01..Q-14, each naming the exact report or tool that would answer it, plus the default taken if unanswered.
suggestions.why_now: The defaults are already being applied; better to list them.
suggestions.risk: None — it is a list.
suggestions.unlocks: Any future session can act without re-asking.

suggestions.title: Own the photos, own the site
suggestions.problem: The one asset a small review site can have that AI cannot fake is a real photo of a real thing on a real counter.
suggestions.change: Buy or borrow the products, shoot four frames each (front, basket, storage, in-use), publish with a caption naming the date and the kitchen, and let the affiliate links follow the trust.
suggestions.why_now: It is also the fastest route to first-hand opinion, which is what the review must be honest about.
suggestions.risk: Cost and time; if the products are not bought, keep saying nothing was tested.
suggestions.unlocks: Differentiation no competitor can copy-paste.

suggestions.title: Keep a “what we did not check” box on every guide
suggestions.problem: Readers increasingly distrust sites that never admit limits, and disclosure-only honesty reads as legal boilerplate.
suggestions.change: One short box per guide naming the specific absence (no test, no price check, no review-sample analysis) with a link to the flagged row.
suggestions.why_now: It converts the site's biggest weakness into a legible standard.
suggestions.risk: Do it once per page, plainly; repeated hedging becomes its own tell.
suggestions.unlocks: Trust with the reader and with the application reviewer.

suggestions.title: Replace the “top pick” frame with a decision frame
suggestions.problem: Rankings require grounds we do not have: no testing, no review corpus, no price data.
suggestions.change: Guides end with “if X matters most, check Y” branching instead of a #1 slot.
suggestions.why_now: It is both compliant with the honesty principle and more useful.
suggestions.risk: Loses the headline number some readers want.
suggestions.unlocks: No fabricated ranking to defend.

suggestions.title: Publish an open data page for the programme
suggestions.problem: A marketing site hides its workings; a publication shows them and survives scrutiny.
suggestions.change: /dashboard/ exposes register, intent records, ledger, flags and cadence as readable tables with source links — dashboard-styled but clearly separate from reader pages.
suggestions.why_now: It is where the owner reviews state without opening a terminal.
suggestions.risk: Never leak secrets here; the page is public. No keys, no account identifiers beyond the tracking ID the owner chose to publish.
suggestions.unlocks: Reviewability.

suggestions.title: Do not automate the second opinion
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for an autonomous agent that identifies high-converting products and optimises campaigns; “high-converting” for a specific product is not knowable from public sources without a corpus and a model.
suggestions.change: Keep product selection a gated step: automation collects and formats; a human approves each claim; the ledger alone justifies re-ranking.
suggestions.why_now: Setting the boundary now is what lets the rest be automated later without fear.
suggestions.risk: Slower catalogue growth — the intended cost.
suggestions.unlocks: Long-term, scalable, defensible automation.
